ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In trapezoid $ABCD$, $AD$ is perpendicular to $DC$, $AD=AB=3$, and $DC=6$. In addition, $E$ is on $DC$, and $BE$ is parallel to $AD$. Find the area of $\triangle BEC$.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the figure, AB is the upper horizontal side, DC is the lower horizontal side, AD is vertical and perpendicular to DC, and BE is also vertical, dropping from B to point E on DC, therefore BE is parallel to AD; ABED forms a rectangle, and on the right side is triangle BEC. Then reason: because ABED is a rectangle, DE=AB=3, BE=AD=3. Also DC=6, so EC=DC-DE=6-3=3. Triangle BEC has EC as its base and BE as its height, and its area is (1/2)×3×3=4.5.

method.method_draft: Use a direct base-height computation for triangle BEC. From the text, use AD ⟂ DC, AD=AB=3, DC=6, E on DC, and BE ∥ AD. From the diagram, identify AB as the top base parallel to DC and BE drawn vertically down to E, forming rectangle ABED. Since ABED is a rectangle, DE=AB=3 and BE=AD=3. Then EC=DC-DE=6-3=3. Triangle BEC has base EC=3 and height BE=3, so its area is (1/2)(3)(3)=4.5.
